adaptations.rationale: The user requires removing Cursor service dependencies while retaining Fabushi cloud capabilities. Reuse the existing native origin authority, identify Fabushi production by exact origin and preserve both development and deliberate-production opt-ins before a dev Host may drain production room events. Foreign/malformed endpoints remain denied even in packaged builds or with both overrides. Existing sharing state and lifecycle owners remain intact; this endpoint fence does not establish native room/relay or packaged sharing acceptance.

Preserves the frozen Grok 0.18 React renderer structure while adapting shipping Fabushi contracts only: browser-login status application is monotonic so a late logging-in acknowledgement cannot overwrite a newer logged-in observation; the root exposes stable Agent-shell markers used by product parity acceptance; empty sidebar-section records fall back to Grok visible-Agent ordering; and complete-roster reconciliation settles an unselected account on the first visible Agent. These adaptations also publish the live sidebar width to the shell so the recovered WindowChrome drag carrier does not overlap Fabushi Agent header controls; the sidebar header remains the local drag surface and its controls are explicit no-drag regions. They keep authentication real through cursorAccount.login/getStatus and keep roster/selection state on the production Coordinator path rather than introducing a parallel renderer. It also preserves optimistic user-message text and committed attachment metadata while correlated authoritative message/attachment echoes settle, so the live transcript does not drop attachment chips between send acceptance and durable echo. Authoritative transcript baselines, updates, and appends are reconciled by message id and client nonce while unioning committed attachment metadata, so transport ordering or a late durable snapshot cannot erase a user's attachment chip after send acceptance. Initial openAgentTail completion is also reconciled with entries that arrived while the initial page request was in flight, preventing a stale first-page response from erasing an optimistic or newly echoed attachment-bearing turn. Transcript feed snapshots also retain only unresolved pending-* user turns that have not yet been correlated by id/clientNonce, so a late empty or stale authoritative baseline cannot erase the optimistic turn between submit acceptance and its durable echo; ordinary non-pending rows remain fully baseline-authoritative. The shipping renderer now also owns the recovered Grok sidebar multi-selection composition: modifier/range selection, clear, and bulk move-to-existing/new-section callbacks are wired to renderer state and the account-scoped sidebarSectionsStore, so the byte-identical sidebar selection UI is reachable without a legacy shell. Phase 1 additionally absorbs Human conversations into this same renderer owner: the existing sidebar/workspace/composer/transcript are reused, Human sends keep the recovered optimistic/reconnect queue, canonical attachment commit path and reply controller, and explicit Human-to-Agent handoff still crosses the established Coordinator-to-Host-to-Runner boundary. No parallel Human shell or message runtime is introduced. Phase 1 reconnect convergence now refreshes an already-open Human transcript from the same Host-owned canonical Session/Transcript immediately after native history sync, while baseline reconciliation preserves unresolved optimistic rows; the Host shipping-client contract separately proves bounded multi-page multi-device gap recovery without a renderer-side message truth. Human older-history loading now reuses the existing transcript pagination controller against a Host gateway that pages the same canonical Human Session SQLite owner; initial Human open syncs native transport then projects only the latest bounded tail, while scroll pagination retains the existing cursor, viewport-anchor, request-fencing, and deduplication ownership. Phase 1 roster recovery further separates local Agent roster readiness from shipping Human convergence: listAgents publishes the canonical loaded/empty Agent state before a potentially slow remote Human sync, while Human sync remains account/transport/attempt fenced, keeps its durable local fallback, and refreshes the active Human transcript after convergence. This prevents Human network latency from holding the canonical Agent shell in an indefinite loading state without weakening either synchronization path. Phase 1 Human reactions now reuse the recovered reaction pills/action surface while mutation and settlement remain Host-owned: the renderer calls the existing Coordinator client, receives the canonical updated Human transcript row, and never creates a reaction store. Human Find-in-chat likewise reuses the recovered find controller and canonical transcript pagination owner: full durable Human search is provided by the Host search gateway, while navigation to an older hit reveals bounded history through the existing pagination controller and virtual transcript handle instead of replacing the timeline with a parallel search result model. Phase 1 additionally routes canonical UI language/accessibility preferences through this existing boundary and applies them to the shipping renderer without creating a parallel settings owner. Restored Human selections are also retried through the same canonical openAgent path once the asynchronous Human roster establishes the conversation type; same-selection reopen remains allowed only while no transcript page is loaded, closing the restart race where a Human id could be briefly addressed through the Agent tail method without introducing alternate state. A successful Host-settled Human send now upserts the authoritative row by canonical id/client nonce, so a concurrent initial-page or roster reconciliation cannot silently erase the accepted backend result from the visible transcript. Human remote-search settlement now promotes the first authoritative match through the existing find controller step path only when no current match exists, so the recovered ordinal/navigation contract and bounded older-page reveal converge without a renderer-side search truth. THEME-I18N-A11Y further keeps this canonical owner while making locale changes immediately visible in the mounted Settings shell, providing locale-sensitive formatting/announcement evidence, and fencing real composition input so CJK/RTL mixed-direction editing cannot submit or be externally overwritten mid-composition. Stop response also settles the renderer running projection only after the canonical Host interrupt call confirms `interrupted: true`, so CHAT-011's packaged acceptance can hide the stop control and accept a subsequent turn without moving operation ownership into the renderer. The shipping renderer removes the obsolete iOS menu entry and keeps account labels consistent with Fabushi branding. The same canonical renderer now exposes Human-message Forward through the recovered ConversationTranscript and a source-neutral ForwardMessageDialog, while execution remains on the existing Coordinator/Host Human Conversation owner; the renderer keeps only dialog, query and settlement projection state and does not become a second Message or Search truth. The explicit 2026-10-24 service-independence requirement routes Help to Fabushi support and Usage to the existing in-app settings owner backed by native token budgets, removing foreign Help/spending navigation without adding renderer account truth. NMR-26 keeps the existing renderer conversation cache and pagination controller as projections of the canonical Host Session/Transcript. Extracted reconciliation helpers preserve loaded history, same-ID updates, nonce acknowledgements and post-request events across initial reads, feed baselines, full refreshes and older-page requests. Only account-scoped history cursors and transient read-update buffers are added; clear, delete, account change and superseded reads invalidate them. Forward activation, recipient search and settlement carry the captured source-entry/account generation through the existing dialog and Host forwarding boundary, including synchronous unmount invalidation and stale roster-response refusal. No second message, search, retry or persistence owner is introduced. NMR-PAGING-01 extends the existing account-scoped history cursor cache and Human history RPC with the Host-issued opaque continuation beside the physical sequence anchor, preserving cached reopen, root-cache handoff and the existing generation fences. Human send-result and live-event reconciliation use the shared author-aware correlation helper so canonical settlement and peer rows remain distinct while the same root cache owns presentation. FPM-UI-CLOSE-01 also gives the existing Plugins overlay a dedicated frame below the reserved WindowChrome control band and above the workspace drag/header layers, passing the band's height to the existing dialog CSS and using no-drag regions. This preserves the current Plugins and window-control owners. Authored shipping-renderer pointer tests cover close/reopen at 1024x684 and 1280x900 with controlled Host/auth and geometry evidence; they do not execute native window-button actions. These source and test mappings do not establish ordinary Human retry completion or an executed visual/package acceptance result. The frozen217 integration retains account-scoped submission reset, author-qualified acknowledgement events, prior-ID mutation reconciliation, guarded reaction settlement, deduplicated initial reads and actual Transcript viewport callbacks. Full-refresh/clear/Find/older-page failures remain on the existing cache and pagination owner. NMR-50d passes the original Forward dialog/account lifetime predicate to the existing Coordinator call after readiness and before its request frame; once posted, existing Host settlement and projection retirement remain unchanged. These source changes do not implement ordinary Human message Retry.

Preserves the frozen Grok ConversationTranscript as the single shipping transcript owner while adding one source-neutral message-action seam: an optional onForward callback. MessageActionAnchor exposes Forward only for settled ordinary messages when the shipping Conversation owner supplies that callback, including attachment-bearing messages, while preserving read-only gating, reply/thread/reaction actions, transcript identity, rendering and lifecycle. ProductionRenderer supplies this callback only for canonical Human conversations and execution crosses the existing Coordinator/Host message owner; no Telegram/ShareBox transcript, route, Message store, or renderer-side forward truth is introduced. The same Transcript now reports its actual mounted viewport by callback, exposes one accessible older-history failure/Retry control, and pauses automatic history reads after failure until explicit retry. ProductionRenderer binds this viewport to the existing pagination and Find owners across initial failure/replacement; it does not query an obsolete DOM node or create another transcript surface. Message Resend remains the separate unclosed Human Retry responsibility. UI-NMR-CURSOR-ACTIVATION-001 reevaluates the existing near-top rule after committed entries change, so an initial unprobed-to-more cursor and a same-hasOlder conversation replacement activate their current continuation without an artificial scroll. Existing loading/failure guards, controller single-flight, viewport callback and layout-phase pending-anchor ownership remain. The actual-root no-scroll case and retained Renderer scenarios are authored recovery evidence; containing-H Actions execution is separate.

Keeps Grok 0.18 Agent projection/filter/sort semantics while accepting the shipping Mahayana Coordinator agents event envelope { agents: [...] } in addition to the frozen direct array form. The adaptation is limited to transport normalization at the renderer projection boundary; Agent identity, hidden state, activity and ordering continue through the frozen Grok projection logic. It also normalizes authoritative Mahayana transcript echoes that carry Grok attachment contexts on user messages, preserving committed path/name/MIME/size metadata for mixed and attachment-only sends without relying on optimistic renderer state. Phase 1 extends this same projection boundary with Human-conversation and Human-transcript normalization while preserving the RendererAgent/ConversationTranscriptEntry contracts, including canonical attachment metadata, reply relation fields and trusted Agent author names. The renderer also maps legacy Grok/Grok Bot default profile names to the Fabushi product label while preserving all other configured Agent names. NMR-49 maps the existing Host dispatching state to the existing renderer pending projection instead of allowing the generic sent fallback. The same decoder is used for ordinary text and attachment message shapes; nonce, reply relation, content and attachment metadata are retained, and established Human/Agent delivery projections remain unchanged. This is presentation normalization of Host-owned settlement, not a new delivery state or renderer-owned send lifecycle. NMR-PAGING-01 projects the Host-issued nextBeforeCursor beside nextBeforeSeq and preserves optional Human authorKind, authorId and remoteMessageId on ordinary message rows for the shared author-aware settlement merge. These fields are Host identity projections rather than credentials or renderer authorization state. Existing dispatching-to-pending and Agent projection semantics remain, and the current model does not interpret lastDispatchError as ordinary retry eligibility. The focused projection and history tests exercise the added identity/cursor shape without claiming a mounted Retry flow. The current Human projection also preserves an explicit empty attachments array, so authoritative resource removal is distinguishable from an omitted partial field. Existing Agent attachment extension remains compatible. Persisted dispatch-error-to-failed projection and full Human Retry are still open.

Preserves the frozen Grok 0.18 account-scoped composer draft store while adapting a shipping race exposed by real desktop attachment staging: a late persistence restore must not overwrite a draft mutation that occurred while the read was in flight. A monotonic mutation revision fences both pre-read and post-read restore settlement without changing account generation semantics, persistence format, or normal draft equality rules. The explicit .ts model import makes this recovered module executable under the Node 24 strip-types contract-test runner while remaining valid under the desktop Bundler TypeScript configuration.

Preserves the frozen Grok 0.18 thin preload boundary while adapting Fabushi's native attachment IPC contract: renderer Uint8Array payloads are encoded to the native bytesBase64 field, rich native staging results are normalized to the recovered {ok,path} contract, and rich committed attachment records are normalized to string paths. Commit requests carry path/name pairs as native items so file names survive the staging-to-committed transition. The shipping preload is bundled from source/electron-preload/runtime/primary.ts by desktop/scripts/build-electron-runtime.mjs; no deleted desktop/electron compatibility root is retained as behavioral or test evidence. Phase 1 additionally routes canonical UI language/accessibility preferences through this existing boundary and applies them to the shipping renderer without creating a parallel settings owner. Phase 1 media/device settings remain on this same canonical Settings/MainEdge/preload owner: selected microphone/camera IDs are normalized and persisted locally, exposed through the existing callMedia bridge, projected by recovered Settings, and consumed by the shipping Human call capture path with stale-device fallback. MP-01..05 additionally routes an optional first-party publisher facet through this same native composition: exact trusted-main sender, current account auth kept internal, bounded OS-selected signed package, account-departure fence and no uncertain-write retry. Backend retains namespace/artifact/review authority; the bridge exposes no reviewer credential, approval or installation runtime. Existing MCP, Coordinator and Host responsibilities are preserved. MU production wiring uses only appId intents and public metadata at the existing MCP owner; Account supplies confirmed authId scope and departure fences, Host retains verification on MainData, and main alone decodes resources into isolated windows. First-party Account and publisher requests use Electron net with no cookies or weakened origin checks. The networkProxy bridge adds only get/mutate calls to the existing typed Main RPC boundary. Proxy preferences and write recovery belong to Rust ProductSettingsOwner through Coordinator MainData, not preload or SandSettingsStore. This bridge can project persisted preferences and the current unavailable publication without claiming an operational Telegram network carrier.

The frozen TipTap composer is preserved semantically, with only Fabushi ownership boundaries around local persistence and voice input. Agent switches fence queued transactions from the previous scope. Browser beforeinput releases the fence before ordinary edits; committed DOM input also performs a one-shot canonical-state rescue when ProseMirror has already reconciled the DOM without emitting an accepted onUpdate, preventing visible prompt text from diverging from the persisted Agent-scoped draft. Programmatic voice/dictation insertion explicitly releases the same fence before insertText. The focused Electron parity E2E reads the real client-persistence slice and guards this ownership boundary. THEME-I18N-A11Y further keeps this canonical owner while making locale changes immediately visible in the mounted Settings shell, providing locale-sensitive formatting/announcement evidence, and fencing real composition input so CJK/RTL mixed-direction editing cannot submit or be externally overwritten mid-composition.

Preserves Grok attachment-gateway behavior while removing a forbidden Electron-main dependency on the legacy TypeScript Host attachment service. Link metadata now crosses the existing Coordinator main leg, and bounded preview-image handling lives in shared media code. This keeps Electron Main, Coordinator and Host as independent Grok-shaped processes while retaining the same attachment/link-preview contract.

Preserves Grok MCP/OAuth composition while keeping SandMcpManager as the single Electron/Coordinator-owned MCP manager and the Mahayana Host as the owner of Plugin Skills lifecycle, cache, authenticated startup, refresh, install/uninstall resync, live-reference cleanup, and Skill Publish. The Cursor Dashboard/marketplace-dependent installed-plugin loader stays as a narrow TypeScript SDK edge in Electron Main and is reached only through the existing allowlisted, correlated Mahayana Coordinator MCP relay. This preserves the frozen Grok process and responsibility boundaries while choosing TypeScript for the Cursor Node SDK edge and Rust for Host lifecycle/state; it does not introduce a second MCP manager or collapse Coordinator/Host/Runner. The approved row-62 MCP discovery failure extension now forwards the frozen success/failure/stale/elapsed settlement through a dedicated reportMcpDiscoveryFailed Coordinator main-data request to the unique HostStructuredLogTelemetry owner; generic MCP diagnostics remain separate. Backend retains namespace/artifact/review authority; the bridge exposes no reviewer credential, approval or installation runtime. Existing MCP, Coordinator and Host responsibilities are preserved. MU production wiring uses only appId intents and public metadata at the existing MCP owner; Account supplies confirmed authId scope and departure fences, Host retains verification on MainData, and main alone decodes resources into isolated windows. First-party Account and publisher requests use Electron net with no cookies or weakened origin checks. Current-main official MCP integration preserves the native Fabushi issuer guard, composes the fixed official provider directory/native vault into the existing MCP facade, and treats foreign legacy Dashboard lookup failure as explicit degraded state rather than broadening account-token origins. The Mini App management subtree now keeps the same dialog parent and sibling position while the ordinary plugin marketplace resolves asynchronously, so an in-flight native install keeps its renderer lifecycle generation instead of being remounted into an empty transient projection; Host installation authority and account fencing remain unchanged.

Keeps the frozen Grok attachment manager semantics while sourcing data-root and path reanchoring from the shared Node boundary rather than legacy Host TypeScript. This is a dependency-direction adaptation only; attachment lifecycle and path semantics remain owned by Electron Main.

Preserves Grok Electron-main Coordinator auxiliary wiring while resolving the Fabushi data directory through shared Node infrastructure instead of importing legacy Host TypeScript. The Coordinator itself remains the independent Rust Mahayana process; this adaptation only cleans the Electron-side dependency edge.

Preserves Grok development box-recreate behavior while moving the data-root dependency to the shared Node layer. This prevents the development control plane from retaining a second legacy Host runtime dependency.

Keeps Grok media-protocol behavior and changes only the path-reanchoring dependency from legacy Host TypeScript to the shared data-root utility, preserving Electron Main ownership of privileged media protocol handling. DMW-01 adds an optional native-only declaration list to this same single pre-ready registration call; the production entry appends the isolated mini-app scheme, without another global registration or changes to sand-media handlers. The default call remains backward compatible.

Preserves the frozen Grok production binding graph while cutting two legacy Host-TypeScript imports: local-exec daemon protocol ownership is now in Electron Main and the data-root resolver is shared. The actual local-exec supervision still belongs to Mahayana Coordinator, so this adaptation strengthens rather than collapses the Grok process boundary. DMW-01 additionally injects the mini-app scheme through the existing MediaProtocol registration owner, with an empty default for existing callers. No second protocol bootstrap, Host or account owner is introduced. EUS-01/03 keeps the existing updater composition and experiment/disposal lifecycle while using configuredUpdateFeedBaseUrl for the same primary/compatibility startup precedence as the service. A present blank FABUSHI_UPDATE_FEED_BASE_URL cannot enable the development feed override through a legacy fallback. This is an explicit-source adaptation, not evidence of an operational release feed.

Preserves Grok desktop user-data bootstrap semantics while moving Fabushi data-root helpers from legacy Host TypeScript into the shared Node layer, so Electron startup no longer depends on a parallel Host implementation. MFA-04 extends this same pre-ready owner with explicit absolute appData/temp overrides and pins the existing Host RuntimeStore and shared profile root beneath the selected appData. Ordinary startup defaults and the existing userData/sessionData owner remain unchanged; no parallel credential store or database is added. The isolated factory consumer selects its verified disposable RAM volume. Focused bootstrap contracts and signed account-transition acceptance remain mandatory.

Preserves Grok startup data-root migration behavior while replacing legacy Host path/lock imports with shared data-root utilities and an Electron-main host-process identity seam. This lets migration safely recognize the shipping Mahayana Host without retaining the old Host runtime implementation.

Keeps Grok local-tool approval persistence semantics while moving the common data-root lookup to shared Node infrastructure. The shipping local-exec lifecycle is supervised by the independent Rust Coordinator; this TypeScript compatibility module no longer owns or imports a Host runtime path.

Preserves the Cursor backend path but deliberately removes the legacy in-process TypeScript provider-session fallback. Any non-Cursor provider must route through Mahayana Coordinator and the independent Host/Runner pipeline, enforcing the required Grok Coordinator/Host/Runner fault and responsibility boundaries rather than keeping a second inference runtime.

Extends the frozen Coordinator-main RPC contract only for approved cross-boundary capabilities: fetchLinkMetadata plus Box MCP load/list-servers/list-tools-raw/execute-tool-raw operations. Electron remains the MCP manager owner; the calls cross the existing Coordinator protocol into the shipping Host/Box implementation with request/reply ownership preserved and no parallel transport channel. Immutable resource bytes remain native-only and no generic transport or renderer installation authority is introduced. The current AppHost persists preferences and returns telegramClientUnavailable without loading a legacy provider; existing attachment/MCP contracts remain in the same table.

Each command fails closed when its Electron owner is unavailable; the Rust Coordinator relay separately freezes the allowlist, request correlation, and failure settlement and contains no Plugin Skills business logic.

Keeps the Grok production Coordinator provider graph while wiring the approved Host MCP lifecycle and Plugin Skills loader calls to the existing Electron ProductionMcpService. This is dependency injection across the established Coordinator boundary: Electron provides the Cursor SDK edge, Rust Host owns Plugin Skills lifecycle/state, and no second manager or in-process Host replacement is introduced. Phase 1 also derives an account-scoped durable Fabushi Human identity only after successful account authorization and passes it through the existing Coordinator bootstrap into Host; account transitions clear that identity. This is identity dependency injection on the existing process graph, not a second communication runtime.

Preserves the frozen Grok production composition while applying two explicit Fabushi product adaptations without moving ownership: the existing Host lifecycle/Plugin Skills SDK-edge surface remains in the single Electron MCP owner, and renderer-scoped BrowserWindow delivery is narrowed at the shipping composition boundary to the trusted main WebContents. The frozen source/electron-main/window-broadcast.ts helper remains byte-identical to Grok for truly global fanout; MCP OAuth completion and dev-control renderer events no longer use that all-window helper in production. Coordinator, Host, Runner, MCP manager, and MainEdge ownership remain unchanged. FDN-001 composes the existing Fabushi Account owner with the existing official device registry at this same production composition boundary: packaged Desktop authenticates only its current Fabushi account session on the outbound /agent WebSocket, account epoch/revoke closes stale registration, and the only newly advertised remote tool delegates read-only status to the existing private App Agent Surface. This creates neither a second device database nor a native executor; exact-head Actions enforce account-switch fencing, bearer non-disclosure, read-only preflight and no retry of stale/write-shaped calls. The existing Coordinator MainData event callback consumes only native-shell web-proxy-bootstrap payloads and delegates them to the strict loopback bootstrap opener through the existing native shell. Invalid URLs and opener failures are reported without creating proxy persistence or a second carrier. ProductSettingsOwner currently reports telegramClientUnavailable, so this retained event-consumer seam does not establish an active Telegram proxy or login path.

Preserves the Grok SandMcpManager implementation as the single MCP owner while exposing approved Fabushi capabilities through the typed desktop facade: force-refresh catalog options, external-auth completion, and Box MCP server loading/tool discovery/tool execution backed by the existing Coordinator→Host Box path. Manager ownership is not duplicated in Rust Host and the Coordinator/Host/Runner failure boundaries remain independent. The approved row-62 MCP discovery failure extension now forwards the frozen success/failure/stale/elapsed settlement through a dedicated reportMcpDiscoveryFailed Coordinator main-data request to the unique HostStructuredLogTelemetry owner; generic MCP diagnostics remain separate. Current-main official MCP integration preserves the native Fabushi issuer guard, composes the fixed official provider directory/native vault into the existing MCP facade, and treats foreign legacy Dashboard lookup failure as explicit degraded state rather than broadening account-token origins.

Preserves the frozen Grok MCP runtime lifecycle while adding only the approved dependency forwarding needed by Fabushi Box MCP parity: loadBoxMcpServers, listBoxMcpServers, listBoxMcpToolsRaw, and executeBoxMcpToolRaw are passed into the single SandMcpManager created by the existing runtime. The approved row-62 MCP discovery failure extension now forwards the frozen success/failure/stale/elapsed settlement through a dedicated reportMcpDiscoveryFailed Coordinator main-data request to the unique HostStructuredLogTelemetry owner; generic MCP diagnostics remain separate.

Preserves the frozen Grok Coordinator runtime ownership/relaunch model while adapting one Fabushi-approved resource-lifetime boundary: the shipping Mahayana Host owns a managed loopback box exec-daemon on a single fixed production endpoint, so renderer-port replacement and explicit Coordinator restart must retire the previous Coordinator/Host generation completely before launching the successor. Intentional retirement is fenced from crash-relaunch accounting, and repeated renderer requests coalesce behind the same generation replacement. This prevents overlapping shipping Host generations from racing for the managed daemon without moving Host or Runner responsibilities into Electron Main or collapsing the independent Coordinator/Host/Runner failure boundaries.

Preserves the frozen Grok MCP tools discovery algorithm while extracting its success/failure settlement into a dependency-free typed helper so the exact success-no-failure-event, cold-failure clear, stale-serving, error-class, and elapsed semantics are executable contracts. The shipping producer still owns discovery/cache settlement; only failure reporting is forwarded through the dedicated Coordinator request to the unique HostStructuredLogTelemetry owner.

Adapts frozen Grok box-copy-in from TypeScript to the Mahayana Host Rust owner without changing process ownership. The real --box-copy-in lifecycle remains the producer; started, slow/stuck watchdog, failed and successful terminal level decisions plus the full frozen metadata shape are preserved. Optional hydrate_source/restored_store_db_entries retain undefined-as-omitted semantics, store_backend remains an identity tag as in the frozen standalone telemetry owner, and every event crosses the single typed HostStructuredLogTelemetry::report_box_copy_in facade into the canonical fixed sand.box_copy_in mapper. Coordinator and Electron gain no second structured-log owner. The user's 2026-10-24 requirement to preserve cloud files on Fabushi-owned services supersedes proprietary transport parity: explicit native mode now injects the same Host native credential owner, selects the existing BoxObjectStore port with CAS/chunk transfer and emits fabushi-native as its backend tag. Native mode does not select the old V2/AgentStore migration fallback; local-FS precedence and copy-in lifecycle/telemetry behavior are retained. Native HTTP/large-object/port contracts passed in Actions 40057785937 at bd647e94; package, sharing/encryption and full release acceptance remain pending.

Preserves the frozen Grok 0.18 Coordinator renderer source except for the explicit Fabushi user-interrupt extension required by the shipping Agent product: interruptAgent is admitted through the closed method table, its {agentId, interrupted} reply is fail-closed validated, and telemetry remains owned by the existing send domain. The production renderer exposes the corresponding Stop response control, while signed packaged acceptance verifies cancellation settles and a fresh post-cancel turn completes; no parallel transport, owner, or legacy shell is introduced. The existing closed Coordinator method table assigns twelve typed legacy Telegram authorization method names to the existing auth telemetry domain. Request transport, failure classification, cancellation, reconnect and episode ownership remain in the recovered Coordinator source. The wrapper records bounded operation/failure metadata rather than authorization arguments. In the current Native composition these historical authorization routes are explicitly unavailable at AppHost; this classification does not reactivate a Telegram provider or establish a second account owner. Shared projection and AppHost refusal tests do not establish direct execution coverage of every telemetry classification. NMR-PAGING-01 maps the Human transcript-page reply kind to the existing shared Human-page parser and assigns getHumanConversationTranscriptTail to the existing transcript telemetry domain. Malformed replies continue through the recovered source's established failure boundary; request transport, pending settlement and telemetry episode ownership are unchanged. This is typed cursor projection and bounded operation classification, not a second history source. Shared-parser and renderer pagination cases do not establish direct coverage of every recovered-source telemetry/failure path.

Preserves the frozen Grok 0.18 inference-router ownership and provider-selection contract while adding one Fabushi product provider identity required by the shipping account boundary. Fresh Fabushi profiles select the first-party provider in product composition; the independent Mahayana Host/Runner reuses the existing Responses lifecycle, tool, checkpoint, usage, and cancellation machinery with the account-bound Fabushi credential and official product endpoint. Cursor, Codex, Claude Code, and OpenRouter retain their original identities and ownership, and the upstream Grok default remains Cursor outside Fabushi composition. This adaptation prevents a Fabushi product bearer from being misrouted to Cursor private backend infrastructure without creating a parallel inference runtime or collapsing Coordinator/Host/Runner responsibility boundaries.

Phase 1 adds canonical Fabushi language/accessibility preferences without introducing a second settings runtime: persistence stays in the existing Electron SandSettingsStore, mutations cross the existing typed MainEdge/preload bridge, and the recovered Settings surface only projects that owner. Locale/direction, reduced-motion, high-contrast controls, and bounded text scaling are normalized fail-closed and applied to the shipping renderer document; account, Coordinator, Host, Runner, theme, and Agent ownership are unchanged. Phase 1 media/device settings remain on this same canonical Settings/MainEdge/preload owner: selected microphone/camera IDs are normalized and persisted locally, exposed through the existing callMedia bridge, projected by recovered Settings, and consumed by the shipping Human call capture path with stale-device fallback. Phase 1 Settings capability decisions stay projected from canonical production owners instead of inventing preference stores: privacy is read from the production account policy; media/device remains a persisted Settings/MainEdge preference; system notifications remain intentionally disabled by the canonical settings store; durable conversation/session/attachment storage keeps its existing app-profile/Host roots; attachment downloads keep native Save As ownership; and window shortcuts keep the fixed Electron owner rather than a global or user-remappable registry. The Settings surface makes those applicable or intentionally non-configurable decisions visible and accessible while existing advanced and update controls retain their established owners. Extends the existing Settings desktop adapter with a networkProxy snapshot obtained through bridge.networkProxy.get and a mutation adapter returning the complete existing canonical mutation envelope. The bridge continues through the established preload/Main RPC and Coordinator MainData legs to Native ProductSettingsOwner. The adapter does not serialize proxy state, open sockets, manage a carrier or create another Settings store. PS-UI-01..05 preserves the complete existing ProductNetworkProxyMutationResult, including the separate publication descriptor. A transient WeakMap retains only one in-flight mutation promise per bridge, establishes the guard before bridge invocation, releases by exact promise identity, and makes canonical reads await a dispatched write before get. It neither caches committed state nor automatically replays uncertain writes. Canonical read errors become a fixed safe Settings fallback; availability classification accepts only explicit available=false as unavailable and otherwise remains unconfirmed. Eighteen authored mounted Settings cases exercise the production adapter; this still does not establish functioning native proxy routing.

This recovered settings panel preserves computer update/reset behavior while replacing legacy product labels with Fabushi.

This recovered settings status copy preserves update and egress behavior while replacing legacy product labels with Fabushi. EUS-05 and EUS-WIN-05 extend the existing Settings update projection with explicit unconfigured/invalid update-source and Windows-publisher reasons. Fixed messages are selected by disabledUpdateMessage and consumed by the existing UpdateSettingsPanel. Update source validation, publisher authorization, installer execution and apply-marker recovery remain in the established Electron update service and installer owners; the renderer neither supplies authority nor falls back to a historical feed or publisher.

Preserves the frozen Grok command-palette search/scoring behavior while adapting canonical participant identity reconciliation required by TDRP Revision 9. The shipping projection deduplicates roster rows by stable participant id, preserves the first slot, and replaces that slot with the newest authoritative row before visible/hidden filtering. This prevents stale and replacement roster objects from appearing as duplicate Search results or projecting contradictory hidden state. The adaptation stays inside the existing command-palette/Search owner and is covered by exact-head focused Search contract evidence plus an independent review job; it does not create a parallel participant or search truth.

Preserves the frozen Grok allowlisted external-URL parsing boundary while adapting TDRP Revision 9 credential containment. Ordinary external URLs strip foreign web-login token parameters from query and fragment, including repeatedly encoded parameter names, while a distinct server-accepted path may preserve the exact URL only when it is HTTP(S), credential-free, and matches the expected first-party origin. The accepted-auth capability remains owned by the Fabushi account adapter and is not exposed to MainEdge. Exact-head focused contract evidence and independent review prove this privilege boundary without weakening the general external-URL gate.

Preserves the frozen Grok Agent Network interaction model while adapting only its layout lifecycle to the canonical Fabushi workspace. When explicit dimensions are absent, the Agent Network region fills its current workspace, ResizeObserver owns live rendered geometry, layout/pan/zoom all consume that measured geometry, and the non-passive wheel listener is rebound when live layout dimensions change. This removes the recovered fixed 760x500 behavior and the stale-listener dependency bug without creating a second shell, state owner, or Agent runtime. Existing region/button accessibility semantics remain intact; the exact-head recovered-foundations contract locks measurement/listener dependencies, while the real Electron parity journey proves parent-fill geometry, aria-pressed state, wheel zoom behavior, and captures responsive Agent Network screenshot evidence. The release workflow now treats this evidence-locked architecture adaptation as a packaging-affecting input, so the same exact HEAD must re-pass the strict architecture gate before signed/notarized packaged acceptance can exist.

Explicit MP-01 exception adds proprietary offline-package publication to the existing Plugins surface, not a separate Mini Apps product root. The recovered connector/skills navigation and lifecycle remain intact. The same publisher panel remains reachable during legacy MCP catalog loading/failure; it owns only transient UI state. Trusted native authentication and fixed package selection own privileged submission; Backend remains namespace, artifact and review authority. No Agent, installation, approval or runtime state moves into React. Contract CI exercises the real signed candidate and account/sender fences; renderer and packaged acceptance remain independent gates. MU-01..05 adds transient management projection in this same dialog, preserving Connector/Skills content. Host owns install state and account isolation; absent native support is explicit, and remove-code retains user data. Current-main official MCP integration preserves the native Fabushi issuer guard, composes the fixed official provider directory/native vault into the existing MCP facade, and treats foreign legacy Dashboard lookup failure as explicit degraded state rather than broadening account-token origins.

Preserves the frozen Plugins dialog, navigation and connector browser while adding one optional first-party publisher presentation slot under MP-01. Existing callers need no change and the view gains no authentication, upload, review or installation authority. This is the user-requested Fabushi Marketplace product adaptation within the single Plugins owner, not restoration of the removed standalone Mini Apps shell. Exact-head renderer/contract and packaged gates must pass before publication is claimed.

DCI-07 and DMW-03 remove the process-wide no-sandbox switch, which would defeat the requested untrusted Mini App isolation even when a new window requests sandbox=true. All existing main startup, singleton, window/preload, GPU and lifecycle behavior remains intact; this does not globally force trusted first-party windows into a different preload mode or change Human calls/browser networking. Each downloaded app uses its own sandboxed no-preload window and partition. Actual Electron and same-source signed package gates must prove this security adaptation; no frozen inventory or reference blob is rewritten.

FDN-001 G12 hardens the existing frozen local-exec path owner rather than creating a parallel file service. Authorized file paths are canonicalized through the nearest-existing real path and rejected when they escape the configured root or cross a filesystem/mount device boundary. This intentionally changes the frozen reference-copy semantics to a reviewed Fabushi TypeScript adaptation; the shipping provider now delegates the actual read/write/staged-commit boundary to the Mahayana Host native file helper, which walks Unix paths with directory handles plus openat/O_NOFOLLOW and Windows paths with RootDirectory-relative NtCreateFile plus FILE_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT; canonical realpath remains only a policy preflight, not the TOCTOU security boundary.

FDN-001 G12 extends the existing shipping local-exec file provider with bounded production safety semantics: canonical path fencing, SHA-256/version conflicts, disk peak-space preflight, and an explicitly chunked upload-start/upload-chunk/upload-commit protocol. Chunks are staged in the target directory with offset/size checks and fsync, hashed incrementally, revalidated against the starting file version/path, and atomically renamed only at commit. The provider keeps the established permission/approval and response transport; the actual filesystem boundary is now enforced by the shipping Mahayana Host native handle-relative/no-follow helper, with cross-platform symlink/reparse swap, traversal, conflict, hash, ENOSPC and atomic-commit acceptance in GitHub Actions.

Preserve all existing MCP IPC, settings sync and permission boundaries while refreshing the canonical Host MCP tool inventory after a tool-disable toggle. Official connector disabled state is stored in its scoped native vault and enforced again at execution. Official provider consent now uses the existing Fabushi account origin through a session-bound broker; native encrypted delivery/refresh/revoke remains on this MCP edge. Existing auth-event broadcast and Host refresh settle the existing Plugins surface, without exposing service tokens in renderer or moving account/Coordinator ownership.

Preserve existing Plugins projection/install/private-skill flows, while independently settling catalog, effective installs and server inventory. Catalog failure remains fatal; unavailable installed/server state produces an explicit warning and leaves available directory data inspectable. Official provider Add bypasses optional manual credentials and uses the existing install/native-auth/external-opener lifecycle; installed entries expose Connect for retry. Required custom/team setup and native permission, token, account and broker boundaries remain intact. Actions verifies ordering, failure propagation and manual/legacy preservation.

Official provider Add bypasses optional manual credentials and uses the existing install/native-auth/external-opener lifecycle; installed entries expose Connect for retry. Required custom/team setup and native permission, token, account and broker boundaries remain intact. Actions verifies ordering, failure propagation and manual/legacy preservation. User-authorized OpenClaw-informed catalog cards, category shortcuts and publisher metadata retain the existing callback contracts. See docs/specs/openclaw-plugin-marketplace-design.md; visual acceptance pending.

The user explicitly requires removing Cursor services while retaining Fabushi capabilities. Preserve native application menu roles, shortcuts, window ownership and feedback callbacks; change only Help Center navigation to the existing Fabushi repository support entry. This is a source-locked product adaptation, not a service-migration or packaged-release acceptance claim.

Preserves the frozen MainData leg ownership, adoption, revocation, live request forwarding and disposal. The semantic extension passes an optional typed event callback into the same Coordinator port client so production Main can consume native-shell bootstrap events. It adds no IPC channel, pending-request owner, persistence or legacy provider; the current AppHost proxy publication is unavailable.

Preserves the existing hello/ready protocol, reply correlation, request map, terminal settlement, cancellation and close behavior. The semantic extension delivers parsed event frames to an optional callback only after ready, rejects premature events as a protocol breach and ignores frames after terminal settlement. Production Main consumes the native-shell seam; no event becomes a second request, message store or proxy authority.

EUS-01..06 and EUS-WIN-03..05 adapt the existing updater state machine to an immutable explicitly configured approved feed and explicit Windows publisher authorization. Existing runtime disable reasons retain precedence; clearing a dynamic gate cannot bypass missing source/publisher authority, and disposal prevents new checks. Manifest fetch rejects redirects and omits private request URLs from HTTP errors. Existing track, download, staging, apply-marker settlement, cancellation and restart owners remain; disabled startup still settles its prior marker. Controlled contracts and native fixture verification do not establish an authorized production feed, signed application install, atomic Windows launch or upgrade/rollback acceptance.

EUS-01/02 removes the historical implicit Cursor feed while preserving the existing explicit feed wire protocol. The primary FABUSHI_UPDATE_FEED_BASE_URL is authoritative even when blank or invalid; the legacy variable is consulted only when the primary is absent. The resolver reuses the existing Fabushi origin authority, retains an approved explicit path, rejects credentials/query/fragment and never invokes the account API default. HTTP errors no longer echo the machine-bearing request URL. Missing configuration remains a visible blocked capability, not a successful update check.

EUS-05 and EUS-WIN-05 extend the existing update telemetry vocabulary with distinct non-retryable source-unconfigured/source-invalid and publisher-unconfigured/publisher-invalid causes. The existing bounded relay, report conversion and explicit payload-field allowlist remain the only telemetry path. Configuration, certificate subjects and private manifest URLs are not added to telemetry; fixed Settings messages are projected from the same disabled state.

EUS-01 and EUS-WIN-01 retain createUpdateServiceWiring as the sole production update-service composition. It forwards the explicit primary/compatibility feed choice, injected platform and raw FABUSHI_WINDOWS_UPDATE_PUBLISHERS_JSON only to the existing Windows installer, while preserving Settings, experiment gates, idle signals, marker store, status and telemetry ports. No renderer configuration or implicit publisher trust is introduced. Runtime operational enablement still requires separately approved feed and publisher configuration.

EUS-WIN-01..06 replaces historical common-name trust with an immutable bounded explicit subject plus DER SHA-256 publisher policy. The existing native PowerShell probe requires a valid embedded Authenticode signature, emits UTF-8 and keeps literal-path quoting and timeout. Before/after hashes, per-path probe generations and one-use launch receipts prevent deterministic replacement or stale-probe resurrection; launch rehash failure returns through the existing spawn-error/marker owner without executing. Current native tests use an ephemeral CI certificate and never launch their fixture; they do not approve a Fabushi publisher, prove hostile same-account atomic launch exclusion, or accept signed package install/rollback.

Preserves the frozen renderer Coordinator client's port ownership, request/reply multiplexing, reconnect handling and disposal while adding typed convenience wrappers and shared reply validation for twelve historical Telegram authorization method names. These wrappers use the existing call boundary and introduce no authorization state, credentials, provider or transport owner. In the current Native AppHost, the corresponding compatibility routes reject through legacy_telegram_unavailable, with registration retaining its established firstName validation precedence; no production frontend consumer of the convenience methods was found at the reviewed target blob. This semantic port records typed compatibility and refusal behavior, not active Telegram login functionality. Shared projection and AppHost refusal matrices do not establish direct port coverage of all twelve convenience methods. NMR-PAGING-01 admits getHumanConversationTranscriptTail arguments through the shared Human-page parser before posting and validates its reply through the shared response parser. Opaque cursors are carried unchanged through the existing call, readiness, request-ID and pending-reply owners; they do not create renderer history authority. Shared parser tests directly cover malformed scope and continuation, while renderer pagination tests cover projection/cache/reopen. The earlier parser/projection tests are adjacent contracts. The current extension adds13 direct real-client/broker/controlled-port cases plus7 actual dialog/client cases, whose execution still requires the containing H. NMR-50d adds an optional synchronous local admission predicate to the same call boundary. It must return strict true after currentReady and before pending registration/post; the callback is not serialized. Old account/dialog/source/unmount lifetimes therefore cannot emit a late mutation frame. Posted work is not cancelled or reinterpreted by later predicate changes, and all existing unguarded calls preserve their transport/reply semantics. ForwardMessageDialog passes the captured original lifetime through the real ProductionRenderer callback; no new account authority or transport exists.

NMR-26 preserves the recovered pagination controller's account/conversation scope, exclusive history cursor, single in-flight request and viewport-anchor responsibilities. A scoped transient update buffer lets live changes to rows in an outstanding older-page read override stale returned values, and an onPageApplied handoff commits accepted rows into the existing renderer root cache. Scope changes, initial/full-page replacement, reset and disposal invalidate stale work. Deferring fetch invocation until inFlight is assigned makes synchronous transport failures retryable without creating a second durable history or message owner. NMR-PAGING-01 carries an optional opaque Human traversal cursor beside the existing sequence anchor, while Agent requests retain their sequence-only form. The same controller retains successful event overlays across failed older-page requests and updates them between failure and retry; successful consumption or scope/reset/initial-page replacement clears them. Request settlement now explicitly checks the captured account slot, and the shared production merge applies author-aware Human settlement rules to older rows and root-cache handoff. The controller remains a transient history/viewport projection of Host membership snapshots, not a durable transcript owner. The frozen217 continuation now keeps previous-ID and author-qualified nonce mutations while waiting for the accepted page before restoring its viewport anchor. Failed-read updates coalesce to the latest payload per identity/alias; distinct explicit alias candidates are retained as deduplicated identity edges and rechecked against the returned row author, including no-nonce collisions. This bounds replay by identities rather than repeated events, preserves Human clears and omitted partial fields, admits the first event arriving after a failure, and clears both overlays on successful consumption or scope/reset/initial-page/capability replacement. The actual production Transcript exposes an explicit Retry and stops automatic retry/Find loops on failure.

NMR-PAGING-01 minimally extends the existing TranscriptMessage presentation contract with optional Human authorKind, authorId and remoteMessageId. The existing production decoder supplies these Host-owned identities, and the shared transcript reconciliation helpers consume them to distinguish peer and local nonces and avoid resurrecting a settled local Human placeholder during older-page reads. Existing Agent rows remain compatible because the fields are optional; no account credential, message store, send lifecycle or retry authority is introduced. The actual projection/pagination contracts contain positive and cross-author/settlement cases; source mapping alone is not execution or product acceptance.

The incoming current-owner adaptation adds reset() to the existing composer submission queue. Account replacement advances its generation, retires queued renderer records and releases the local per-agent lane without cancelling any Host-admitted work. Disposal reuses that same retirement operation. ProductionRenderer supplies account-scoped submission records and invokes reset through its existing account lifecycle; late outcomes cannot requeue a prior account or block a fresh account behind its unresolved response. Existing send, offline queue, failure and Agent semantics remain on the original owner. The actual renderer fixture covers queued and in-flight account replacement; these authored contracts do not implement Human message Retry or prove complete packaged acceptance.
